title: The hand-operated Bielenberg ram press, invented to address a cooking oil shortage in Tanzania, has gained popularity in the northern sunflower belt and is attracting interest from other African nations. This innovative press allows villagers to produce sunflower oil for personal use and sale, leading to improved diets, increased incomes, and job creation. The press is user-friendly, easy to maintain, and has been particularly beneficial for farmers, who have reported increased milk production by using the nutritious residue from oil extraction as animal feed. Initially, the project aimed to install large oil presses, but the smaller, hand-operated model proved more effective for rural areas without electricity. The project has seen significant growth, with oil production skyrocketing from 5,000 liters to over 100,000 liters in just three years. The initiative is now expanding to other regions, with a focus on empowering women to participate in oil production.
